fields.reasoning: The question is whether the decision and the parent statements contradict. run-status-tokens says run status shows each session's journaled token use; session-journal says the journal holds token use and status shows it. Neither says status shows only journaled use, and both stay true for sessions that have a journaled reading. The decision adds read-time counts only where no reading is journaled, and it says they are not journaled, so the journal statement stays exact. Amending the parents would put a narrowing or widening into a change set whose intent is only that status never says 'no token use recorded' for a session that used tokens. The arbiter may only write this one decision, so no amendment is made here; if the owner wants the parent statements to name the fallback, that is a separate change set.
fields.statement: The parent statements of run-status-tokens and session-journal stay as written and true. The transcript-read counts of printout-reads-transcript-when-unjournaled are shown only for a session with no journaled reading, so run status shows journaled use for every session that has one, and the counts read at print time are an extra line for a session without one. Neither parent is amended in this change set, and no leaf may say the journal holds those read-time counts.
